title: SME Vendor Onboarding Q&A + Attestation (Lite)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a lightweight onboarding questionnaire and attestation template intended for small suppliers, consultants, and software vendors (SMEs) where a full vendor security assessment would be disproportionate to risk and effort. Use when: vendor handles limited customer data, provides SaaS with no customer data exports, or integrates via a constrained API key.

How to use this file (operational notes):
- Security owner fills in minimum acceptable responses below and marks any mandatory follow-ups.
- Legal will convert the attestation items into a short addendum for low-risk engagements or incorporate into the SOW/DPA as a short annex.
- If answers deviate from minimums, escalate to SRE/Security for either deeper assessment or contract conditions (see "escalation matrix").

SECTION A — Administrative info (to be completed by vendor)
1) Vendor legal name and address:
   - [VENDOR NAME]
   - [REGISTERED ADDRESS]
2) Primary technical contact (name, email, phone)
3) High-level description of services provided to Redwood: (one sentence)
4) Expected data classes accessed or processed for Redwood (pick all that apply):
   - Non-personal config/metadata (e.g., model IDs, runtime parameters)
   - Pseudonymized telemetry
   - Personal data (name, email, customer content) — if yes, flag for escalation
   - Sensitive personal data (PII special categories) — automatic escalation

SECTION B — Architecture & operations (short answers)
1) Where are your production services hosted? (cloud provider + region)
2) Do you host any customer data in persistent storage under your control? (yes/no) If yes, describe encryption at rest and key management approach.
3) Does Redwood connect via public internet, VPN, or VPC peering? Provide auth mechanism (API key / mutual TLS / OAuth / other).
4) Do you use subcontractors/subprocessors to process customer data? (yes/no) If yes list names and purpose (if small list) or provide category.
5) Do you retain logs containing customer data? Describe retention window and mechanism to delete on request.

SECTION C — Baseline security checks (yes / no + short details)
- Do you require/make use of multi-factor authentication for admin accounts?
- Are production credentials rotated on a schedule or when an individual leaves?
- Do you maintain a documented vulnerability management process (patching / disclosure)?
- Is TLS 1.2+ applied to all in-transit data?
- Do you operate an incident response process with defined SLAs for notification?

SECTION D — Minimal evidence requested (attach 1–3 items)
- Screenshot of admin console showing MFA requirement OR written policy excerpt
- Short diagram of network boundaries showing where Redwood data flows (redacted ok)
- Export of last 12 months vulnerability scan summary (high/critical counts only)

SECTION E — Attestation (vendor to initial/checkbox & sign below)
By signing below the vendor attests to the following (tick required for each):
[ ] We will process Redwood customer data only for the purposes set out in the agreement and not for model training or secondary uses unless explicitly permitted in writing.
[ ] We will notify Redwood within 72 hours of becoming aware of a confirmed data breach affecting Redwood data and will provide timely status updates until resolution.
[ ] Access to Redwood-related systems will be limited to employees and subprocessors with a demonstrated business need, and we maintain records of access.
[ ] When we engage subprocessors, we contractually impose obligations materially equivalent to these attested commitments.
[ ] We will delete or return Redwood data within the timeframe required by contract (default 30 days) following contract termination and will certify deletion upon request.

Signature block (digital signature acceptable)
Vendor authorized signatory: ____________________  Date: __________
Printed name / title: ___________________________

SECTION F — Suggested condensed contractual clauses for low-risk SME engagements
(legal: these are starter snippets; adapt per jurisdiction and business needs)
1) Permitted processing & prohibition on model training
   "Vendor shall process Customer Data only to provide the Services and shall not use Customer Data to train, improve, or benchmark models, or for any other machine learning purpose, without Customer's prior written consent."

2) Data security baseline
   "Vendor will implement and maintain administrative, physical, and technical safeguards appropriate to the nature of the Customer Data, including industry standard encryption at-rest and in-transit, MFA for admin access, and documented patching processes."

3) Breach notification and cooperation
   "Vendor shall notify Customer without undue delay and in any event within seventy-two (72) hours after becoming aware of a Security Incident affecting Customer Data. Vendor will cooperate with Customer's reasonable requests to investigate and remediate the incident."

4) Subprocessors
   "Vendor may engage subprocessors provided Vendor gives Customer prior notice of new subprocessors and maintains a written agreement with subprocessors that imposes obligations no less protective than those in this Agreement."

5) Deletion and return
   "Upon termination or expiration of the Agreement, Vendor will, at Customer's election, return or irreversibly delete Customer Data within thirty (30) days and certify completion."

6) Audit rights (limited)
   "For low-risk SME engagements the parties agree to a limited audit: Customer may request a remote review of Vendor's attestation evidence and a representative set of controls, not more than once per 12 months, subject to reasonable confidentiality protections."

7) Liability and insurance (short form)
   "Vendor's aggregate liability for claims arising from the processing of Customer Data shall be limited to direct damages up to the greater of $50,000 or the fees paid in the prior 12 months, except for willful misconduct or gross negligence. Vendor shall maintain cyber insurance with limits not less than $1,000,000."

SECTION G — Red flags (immediate escalation to security + legal)
- Vendor refuses to attest to non-training of models when processing customer content.
- Vendor cannot or will not provide simple encryption/rotation evidence for persistent customer data.
- Vendor uses >3 unknown subprocessors without a mechanism for prior notice.
- Vendor requests broad rights to sublicense, resell, or otherwise repurpose customer content.

SECTION H — Risk decision matrix (for reviewer)
- Green (acceptable, proceed with Lite DPA): vendor processes only non-sensitive data, attests to non-training, provides requested evidence, and uses standard auth.
- Amber (conditional): vendor processes personal data but has documented controls; require specific contract addendum (e.g., shortened breach SLA, data locality clause).
- Red (reject / full assessment): vendor processes sensitive personal data, cannot attest to key controls, or engages high-risk subprocessors.

SECTION I — Implementation checklist for security reviewer
- Confirm host location and data residency requirements met
- Verify MFA screenshot or policy excerpt attached
- Verify encryption at rest statement and KM approach (customer-managed key where required)
- Confirm breach notification time is acceptable and escalation path captured
- If any red flags, flag Legal and Solutions Eng for further contract terms or full questionnaire

Appendix 1 — Example short email template to vendor when requesting this lite onboarding pack:
Subject: Redwood - Quick Onboarding Pack Request
Hi [Vendor Contact],
Thanks for working with Redwood. To complete our lightweight onboarding for SME suppliers, please complete the attached short questionnaire and provide the minimal evidence items listed. If you believe any of the attestation points are not applicable, please explain. We aim to complete this within 5 business days.
Best,
[Redwood Security]

Appendix 2 — Notes to Legal (drafting pointers)
- Consider adding an explicit carve-out for aggregated, de-identified usage metrics if vendor requests to keep telemetry for product improvement, but require strong de-identification.
- If vendor requests model-training rights, require explicit opt-in, narrow scope, and an additional revenue/compensation clause.
- Preferred local law: include clause for injunctive relief for misuse of customer content where applicable.

Change log
- 2024-03-18 Priya M: initial draft (SME/lightweight focus).
- 2024-04-02 Marcus L: added attestation checklist, red-flag matrix, and brief clause snippets.

Unresolved items / open questions
- Threshold for "SME" vs. when to require full vendor-security-assessment (propose $X ARR or access to PII > Y records).
- Insurance minimums: confirm if $1M is acceptable across regions or needs localization for EMEA customers.

End of document
